entries.citation: 742ebdf69 (SD_PATTERNS' featuring discount, no word boundary, Sept 2010); 7b59604c5 (partial fix, beets 2.13.0); 19d091440 (symmetric word-boundary fix, still unreleased at pinned 2.13.1)
entries.reproduced_reason: Reproduced by all six probe cases (Task 16). Each pairs two genuinely different strings that share a leading word ending in "ft" ("Draft", "Left", "Gift", "Soft", "Craft", "Theft"), so SD_PATTERNS' unbounded featuring trigger deletes the rest of both strings and charges the real difference at 0.1. Every case's derived recommendation is strong/apply; recomputed with a word boundary before the trigger, every case's distance lands past strong_rec_thresh (0.04) in the medium band, so all six move the verdict. Per case, derived against defect-free distance: adv-ft-draft-colon 0.010185 / 0.101852; adv-ft-left-colon 0.011765 / 0.117647; adv-ft-gift-space 0.010784 / 0.107843; adv-ft-soft-onesided 0.030095 / 0.086667; adv-ft-craft-titles 0.009171 / 0.091708; adv-ft-theft-artist 0.009091 / 0.090909. The six span the album, track_title, and artist components, both the symmetric and the one-sided firing, and all three members of the trigger's `[\. :]` separator class.

entries.reproduced_reason: Reproduced by all four probe cases (Task 16). Each pairs a release against its own remix or alternate version, with the only distinguishing token inside the 0.3-weight parenthetical (or its square-bracket twin), so the discount erases the differentiator. Every case's derived recommendation is strong/apply; recomputed with the parenthetical at full weight, every case lands past strong_rec_thresh (0.04) in the medium band. Per case, derived against defect-free distance: adv-remix-both-sides 0.024000 / 0.080000; adv-remix-onesided 0.021429 / 0.071429; adv-remix-bracket 0.027778 / 0.092593; adv-remix-track-titles 0.024561 / 0.081871. The four span both bracket patterns, the one-sided and both-sides firings, and the album and track_title components.

entries.citation: #1916 (romaji transliteration, open since 2016); #6358 (locale aliases ignored after mbsync, 2026)
entries.reproduced_reason: Reproduced by two of the four real-catalog non-Latin cases Task 4 already committed (folded here per the Task 17 escalation ruling, which deleted the four byte-identical adv-alias-* duplicates those cases had spawned). _parse_artist_credits (beetsplug/musicbrainz.py:301-331) always reads el['artist']['name'], the MusicBrainz ARTIST ENTITY's own canonical name, never el['name'], the specific RELEASE's own credited display string; when the two diverge in script the applied artist silently discards what the release itself documents, the mechanism #1916 and #6358 both point at from opposite directions (romaji/locale transliteration never selected; a locale alias ignored after mbsync). real-nonlatin-girls-generation (release credits the Korean 소녀시대 per seed-items --facts, but distance 0.076471 applies the Latin "Girls' Generation" instead, artist the sole nonzero penalty, medium/skip) and real-nonlatin-anna-vissi-essential (release credits the Latin "Anna Vissi", but distance 0.014493 applies the Greek Άννα Βίσση instead, matching a documented locale=el alias exactly, artist the sole nonzero penalty, strong/apply) show the entity-name-over-release-credit substitution firing in both script directions, proving it is not a directional bias but a structural gap: the release's own metadata is never consulted for this field at all. The other two real-nonlatin-* cases named above (alla-pugacheva-vol1, x-japan-art-of-life) show no divergence at all: each release's own credited display already equals the artist entity's canonical name, so the applied string happens to match what the release documents, and neither is counted toward this reproduction. Separately, as a scoping finding rather than a reproduction: _preferred_alias (musicbrainz.py:128-155) is structurally unreachable under both the estate and stock profiles, since it iterates config['import']['languages'], empty in both, so `next(matches, None)` returns None unconditionally and no alias is ever even considered a candidate string. This unreachability is not itself counted as reproducing the hypothesis here (no case above shows a nonzero divergence attributable to it, since each release's own alternate-script aliases were unneeded once the credited display already matched); Task 18's locale profile probes this mechanism directly by toggling import.languages against the same alias data.
entries.reason: The Task 17 escalation ruling folded the four adv-alias-* probe cases into their byte-identical real-nonlatin-* twins already committed by Task 4, narrowing the reproduction claim to the two cases whose applied string actually diverges from the release's own credit. Disposition stays owner-only.

entries.citation: #2981 (open since 2018, same track count with divergent titles yields a confidently wrong per-track assignment); #6078 (2025, tracks detected in wrong order)
entries.reproduced_reason: Reproduced by all six probe cases (Task 17). Each gives its item set the same track count as the candidate, an item title held constant across every item (a shared prefix identical to the album's own generic session-tape/take/reel naming, carrying zero per-track content), which string_dist scores identically regardless of which candidate track it is paired against -- title is thereby proven, not merely asserted, to contribute equal weight to every possible pairing -- and adjacent-track lengths tuned so lap.lapjv's own minimum-cost solve prefers a wrong pairing over the correct one. assign_items never rejects a pair; it always returns the minimum-cost total mapping, so the wrong assignment is not a near-miss the solver settled for, it is the solver's own provable optimum. Every case's album-level verdict lands strong/apply despite the wrong per-track mapping (adv-assign-swap-session-tape distance 0.016667 vs. 0.052222 the correct pairing would have scored; adv-assign-swap-field-recording 0.016 vs. 0.048; adv-assign-cycle-rehearsal-reel 0.019481 vs. 0.070390, a genuine 3-cycle among tracks 0-1-2 rather than a simple pairwise swap; adv-assign-double-swap-broadcast 0.021429 vs. 0.032540, two independent adjacent swaps in one 6-track record; adv-assign-endpoint-swap-demo-pass 0.026667 vs. 0.106667, a swap between the release's first and last track rather than adjacent positions, proving the defect keys on length proximity, not index proximity; adv-assign-tight-margin-archive-disc 0.016667 vs. 0.022593, the narrowest correct-vs-wrong margin of the six). Every case's own claims.json pins the wrong assignment explicitly (Assignment plus AppliedFields.title per swapped item); every one is confirmed a unique optimum by the ties ledger (TieMargin 1e-9), not a tie the tie machinery had to disposition.
entries.reason: assign_items never rejects a pair; it always maps every input track onto some candidate track, so the album-level verdict can still land strong while individual AppliedFields.title values are wrong.

entries.bug_class: locale-specific artist alias silently ignored (distinct from bug-nonlatin-alias-selection's entity-name-over-release-credit substitution: this hypothesis targets _preferred_alias itself, gated by import.languages)
entries.reproduced_reason: Read via `gh issue view 6358 --repo beetbox/beets` before authoring (Global Constraints' sanctioned non-/ws/2 read). The report and its thread implicate MusicBrainzPlugin's own album_info/track_info -> _parse_artist_credits -> _preferred_alias chain (beetsplug/musicbrainz.py:128-155, 301-357), which mbsync and the importer's own candidate-building both call identically; the issue is not mbsync-scoped, so the hypothesis was probed rather than filed not-attempted. The two sibling cases share byte-identical Input.Items and responses/, differing only in profile: estate (import.languages: [], today's default) versus locale (estate.yaml plus import.languages: [ja] and import.ignored_alias_types: []; corpus/profiles/locale.yaml, re-based on estate rather than stock so the pair differs by exactly these two keys, per the conductor's Task 18 escalation ruling). Both siblings derive the same best_album_id, recommendation (medium), action (skip), and the winning candidate's own artist penalty (0.072222, the sole nonzero key) -- confirming the profile swap changed nothing about candidate selection or the applied verdict. Within applied_fields, artist, albumartist, artist_credit, and albumartist_credit read identically in both records ("宇多田ヒカル" / "Hikaru Utada"), because bug-nonlatin-alias-selection's own mechanism already sources the artist entity's canonical name for those fields regardless of import.languages, leaving no headroom for _preferred_alias to move them further. Where headroom exists -- artist_sort, albumartist_sort, artists_sort, and albumartists_sort, which under estate all read the Latinized "Utada, Hikaru" (the artist entity's own default sort_name) -- the locale sibling shows all four shift, on every one of the 12 items, to うただヒカル, the sort_name carried by the release's own documented locale=ja alias (confirmed via `harness seed-items --facts`). A second, independent confirmation appears outside applied_fields entirely: candidates[4] (album_id 2375a576-650b-47fb-939b-7c15afc989eb) and candidates[5] (album_id a87189fd-0c95-4f0a-8ad4-4a8638ff11e0), two non-winning candidates both credited to the MusicBrainz "Various Artists" entity, shift their own distance/penalties/tracks values slightly under locale (candidates[4] distance 0.8526610380899999 -> 0.8527205991251707; candidates[5] distance 0.8552206833722313 -> 0.8540534617687298), because "Various Artists" also carries a primary locale=ja alias (ヴァリアス・アーティスト): _preferred_alias fires for these two candidates as well, and for them it substitutes artist_object['name'] itself (musicbrainz.py:317-331), not merely the sort field, moving their own scoring inputs. Neither candidate is within reach of displacing the winner (both sit above 0.85 against the winner's 0.072222), so this is a second, un-asked-for firing of the same mechanism rather than a verdict concern -- but it means the true divergence between the two records is not confined to sort-name fields alone, a finding recorded here rather than smoothed over. That the mechanism is only reachable when import.languages carries a matching locale is the direct evidence it is functioning at pinned beets 2.13.1, contradicting #6358's report that a locale alias is silently ignored.
entries.reason: Written by an agent and left at pending-adjudication: disposition is owner-only (M6), even though the evidence points one way. The two case ids are the evidence that _preferred_alias works at 2.13.1, for Geoff to confirm as oracle-correct.
